EV/EBITDA.name: ebitda_expensed_investment_gap
EV/EBITDA.mechanism: The gap between gross margin and EBITDA margin is the operating expense base (SG&A, marketing, R&D) that is expensed even though much of it builds customer and brand capital, so firms with a large gap have depressed current EBITDA relative to their economic earnings and high operating leverage, and trade at higher EV/EBITDA. Matching 3-digit industry peers on both margins at once (rather than gross margin alone) equalizes this expensed-investment share and the scope for margin expansion, while growth and net leverage match duration and financial risk.
EV/EBITDA.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank gross_margin 1, ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

EV/Sales.name: sales_crossindustry_profitability_twins
EV/Sales.mechanism: Once margins, growth and capital intensity are matched, firms produce similar free cash flow per dollar of sales, whatever their SIC code. Searching the whole cross-section for profitability twins gives a larger and closer-matched peer set than industry codes, which often group businesses with very different economics.
